# 0001. Ref + Open Host Service jako standardowy wzorzec granic międzymodułowych

## Status

Proponowany

## Kontekst

- Driver D2: moduły/zespoły nie mogą się wzajemnie blokować przy wydaniu.
- [ADR-0000](./0000-podzial-na-moduly-domenowe.md) wprowadził granice modułów, ale odłożył budowę ACL
  między nimi na później, per relacja.
- [Context Map](../context-map/context-map.md) nazywa kilka takich relacji opartych na surowym ID bez
  warstwy tłumaczenia (Catalog→Pricing, Catalog→Promotions, Catalog→Warehouse & Suppliers,
  Pricing→Promotions) — w każdej z nich konsument zależy od pełnego modelu i stanu dostawcy, więc
  zmiana kształtu danych po stronie dostawcy może po cichu złamać konsumenta.
- Pierwszy konkretny przypadek: Pricing zależy dziś bezpośrednio od pełnego modelu `Category` i
  wewnętrznego stanu Catalog.

## Decyzja

Ustanawiamy trwały wzorzec dla **wszystkich** granic międzymodułowych z Context Map (obecnych i
przyszłych): moduł-dostawca publikuje minimalną, tylko-do-odczytu projekcję swojego modelu (**Ref**)
jako Open Host Service — jawny, publiczny kontrakt. Warstwa tłumaczenia zawsze leży po stronie
dostawcy, nie konsumenta; konsument zależy wyłącznie od Ref, nigdy od pełnego modelu ani wewnętrznego
stanu dostawcy.

Pierwsze zastosowanie: Catalog publikuje `CategoryRef` (identyfikator + nazwa), Pricing przestaje
zależeć od pełnego modelu `Category`. Plan wdrożenia i checklist:
[docs/migrations/2026-09-02-category-ref-ohs-handoff.md](../migrations/2026-09-02-category-ref-ohs-handoff.md).

Branding identyfikatorów pozostaje świadomie odłożony jako osobny, niepotwierdzony problem.

- **ACL po stronie konsumenta** — odrzucone: i tak wymaga zależności od pełnego modelu dostawcy, gorzej

- **Branding identyfikatorów zamiast Ref** — odrzucone: inny problem (unikalność identyfikatorów),

# Handoff: Category → CategoryRef OHS export (Catalog → Pricing decoupling)

> Status: Phase 1, 2, 3 done.
> Related: [ADR-0001](../adr/0001-category-ref-open-host-service.md), [ADR-0000](../adr/0000-podzial-na-moduly-domenowe.md), [context-map.md](../context-map/context-map.md) (hotspot: Catalog→Pricing raw ID, no ACL).

## Goal

Stop `product-pricing` from depending on Catalog's full `Category` aggregate. `product-catalog`
publishes a minimal `CategoryRef { id, name }` as an Open Host Service (OHS) export; `product-pricing`
consumes only that projection.

Branded/nominal ID types were explicitly **deferred** (out of scope) — `categoryId` stays a plain
`ID` (string) alias. See conversation history for the reasoning (Ref DTOs alone satisfy the
ADR-0000 "no ACL" concern; branding solves a separate, unrelated id-mixup risk).

## Phase 1 — DONE

Implemented as a **separate ACL mapper file**, without touching existing internal module code
(`types.ts`, `api/categories.ts` untouched):

- Created [product-catalog/acl/categoryRef.ts](../../retail-operations-portal/src/modules/product-catalog/acl/categoryRef.ts):
  - `CategoryRef { id: ID; name: string }` — the published-language projection of `Category`.
  - `toCategoryRef(category: Category): CategoryRef` — private mapper.
  - `listCategoryRefs(): Promise<CategoryRef[]>` — calls existing `listCategories()` and maps results.
- Updated [product-catalog/index.ts](../../retail-operations-portal/src/modules/product-catalog/index.ts) to export
  `CategoryRef` (type) and `listCategoryRefs`.
- Verified: `npm run lint` (0 errors) and no TS errors on the two touched files.

Nothing else was changed — `product-pricing`'s pages still read the full `Category` type and
Catalog's own `categoriesSlice` directly (this is what Phase 3 fixes).

# Plan: Fix @ross-org/product-catalog alias

## Context
- `tsconfig.json` has `"@ross-org/product-catalog": ["./src/index.ts"]` — target file doesn't
  exist (no `src/index.ts`); real public API is `src/modules/product-catalog/index.ts`.
- Alias is only used once, in `PricingRulesPage.tsx` (`import { listCategoryRefs } from
  "@ross-org/product-catalog"`). Every other cross-module import in the codebase uses
  `@/modules/product-catalog` instead (routes.tsx, store.ts, PricingRuleForm.tsx,
  PromotionWizardPage.tsx, categoryRefsSlice.ts, WarehousePage.tsx).
- Alias resolution needs 3 consistent places (confirmed by how `@/*` is currently wired):
  1. `tsconfig.app.json` paths — TS compiler (`tsc -b`) / IDE intellisense for src files
     (this is the config with `"include": ["src"]`; root `tsconfig.json` has `"files": []` +
     only `references`, so it's never the active project for src compilation).
  2. `tsconfig.json` paths — used by `eslint-import-resolver-typescript` (configured in
     eslint.config.js via `import/resolver: { typescript: {...} }`, no explicit `project`,
     defaults to root tsconfig.json) — needed for `boundaries/dependencies` rule to resolve
     the specifier to a real file and classify it under the `product-catalog` boundary type.
  3. `vite.config.ts` `resolve.alias` — Vite doesn't read tsconfig paths natively; needed for
     actual dev-server/build runtime resolution.
- Currently only (1) exists, with the wrong target. (2) and (3) are missing entirely, so the
  import is broken end-to-end (lint resolver fails, dev server/build would fail to resolve it).
- Since `product-catalog/index.ts` is the module's public API (per ADR-0000 boundary), pointing
  the alias there is fine — the boundaries deep-import-ban rule already exempts `index.ts`.

## User decisions
- Make `@ross-org/product-catalog` actually work (not revert the one import to
  `@/modules/product-catalog`).
- Scope limited to `product-catalog` only — do NOT add the pattern for
  product-pricing/sales-fulfilment/platform now.

## Steps
1. `tsconfig.app.json` — add `"@ross-org/product-catalog": ["./src/modules/product-catalog/index.ts"]`
   to `compilerOptions.paths`, alongside the existing `"@/*": ["./src/*"]`.
2. `tsconfig.json` — fix the existing (wrong) entry's target to
   `"./src/modules/product-catalog/index.ts"` (same value as step 1). *Parallel with step 1.*
3. `vite.config.ts` — add a `resolve.alias` entry mapping `@ross-org/product-catalog` to
   `path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, './src/modules/product-catalog/index.ts')`, next to the
   existing `'@'` alias. *Parallel with steps 1–2.*
4. No change needed to `PricingRulesPage.tsx` — its import already uses
   `@ross-org/product-catalog`; it just needs the alias to actually resolve.

## Relevant files
- `retail-operations-portal/tsconfig.app.json` — add missing paths entry.
- `retail-operations-portal/tsconfig.json` — fix wrong target path.
- `retail-operations-portal/vite.config.ts` — add resolve.alias entry.
- `retail-operations-portal/src/modules/product-pricing/pages/PricingRulesPage.tsx` — no edit,
  consumer of the alias (context only).
- `retail-operations-portal/src/modules/product-catalog/index.ts` — the alias target, already
  exports `listCategoryRefs`/`CategoryRef` (no edit needed).

## Verification
1. `npm run lint` in `retail-operations-portal/` — expect 0 errors (confirms
   `boundaries/dependencies` resolves the new alias correctly via the ESLint TS resolver).
2. `npx tsc -b` (or `-p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit`) — expect no errors (confirms TS path
   mapping resolves).
3. `npm run dev` (or `build`) and load `/pricing-rules` — category dropdown should populate,
   confirming Vite resolves `@ross-org/product-catalog` at runtime.

## Decisions
- Scope excludes adding this alias pattern for the other 3 domain modules (explicit user choice).
- Root `tsconfig.json`'s paths block is kept (not deleted) because it's the config actually read
  by the ESLint TS resolver by default — not dead code as it first appears.

**Short answer: yes, `eslint.config.js` needs a fix, and no, a "block `../packages` from `src`" rule wouldn't be a real substitute.**

Why not the narrower fix: `eslint-plugin-boundaries` resolves every import specifier to its actual file, then classifies that file against the `boundaries/elements` patterns — it doesn't care whether the import was written as `@/modules/product-catalog/...`, `@ross-org/product-catalog`, or a relative path. Since almost all cross-module imports here are alias-based (not relative `../packages/...` from `src`), a rule that only blocks relative traversal out of `src` would miss:
- the actual deep-import-ban policy (`fileInternalPath: "!index.ts"`) for any alias-based import,
- the directional matrix (`product-pricing ✗→ sales-fulfilment`, etc.) for imports that happen entirely between two `packages/*` folders, with no `src` involved at all.

The real fix is just updating the stale patterns to match where the files actually live now:
</details></think>

- `@ross-org/<moduł>` → `packages/<moduł>/index.ts` — jawny, org-scoped alias na publiczne API
